newsitem.title: USA: U.S. West spot natgas rises, Gulf swing softens.
newsitem.headline: U.S. West spot natgas rises, Gulf swing softens.

text.p: U.S. September spot natgas prices turned stronger in the West on Friday, but talk of swing gas prices in the Gulf were significantly below index levels, industry sources said.
At the southern California border, prices gained about five cents into the mid-to-high $1.70s per million British thermal units as air-conditioning demand picked up on the West Coast.
Similarly in the San Juan basin, prices strengthened into the low-$1.60s as West Coast customers demanded more gas following the Labor Day holiday weekend.
In the Permian basin, however, prices held fairly steady around $1.50, but most traders said they finished their September 1 business on Thursday.

Although baseload prices were still talked in the mid-to-high $1.70s on the U.S. Gulf Coast pipes, prices for the first few days of the month fell to about $1.70 as cooler temperatures were expected in south Texas and parts of the Southeast.
In the Midcontinent, swing prices for September 2 and 3 delivery were talked in the mid-to-high $1.60s, but most traders were absent from the market.
Forecasters are calling for fairly normal temperatures to continue through the early part of next week.
Baseload bidders emerged at the Chicago city-gate at $1.80, down about 10 cents from index levels. At the Detroit city-gate, baseload prices hovered in the $2.05-2.09 area.
Hurricane Edouard was losing steam as it headed north, forecasters said, adding that the storm's threat to the Atlantic Coast was unlikely.
In the distance were Hurricane Fran and Tropical Storm Gustav, which were still far from land.
Fran, packing winds of 75 mph, was heading north-northeast toward the island of Antigua this morning. Gustav was about 970 miles west of the Cape Verde islands.
